 About the role: 
The AVP, Security Architecture is a senior leader accountable for the enterprise security architecture strategy, governance, and evolution of security capabilities across global business and technology environments. 
The role translates business priorities, cyber risk appetite, and emerging threats into architecture direction that protects clients, employees, information, and critical services.
Working closely with the CISO, CTO, enterprise architects, and business technology leaders, the AVP leads the Security Architecture function and embeds secure-by-design, Zero Trust, and defense-in-depth principles into enterprise transformation and solution delivery.
The AVP serves as a senior security design authority within enterprise architecture governance, shapes security investment priorities, and develops a team that provides consistent architectural guidance across business units and geographies.
 What You Will Do?
Key Responsibilities:
 1. Enterprise Security Architecture Strategy and Road mapping 
 Own the enterprise security architecture strategy and target state across identity, cloud, infrastructure, networks, endpoints, applications, data, and security platforms.
 Establish multi-year security capability roadmaps aligned with business priorities, enterprise architecture, the cybersecurity strategy, and organizational risk appetite.
 Translate capability assessments, threat trends, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework into prioritized architecture improvements, with Zero Trust and defense in depth guiding modernization.
 2. Security Architecture Function and People Leadership 
 Lead and develop the Security Architecture team, with accountability for performance, coaching, succession planning, and the skills required to support enterprise priorities.
 Define the function's operating model, engagement processes, and service expectations, providing architecture coverage across security programs and business-led technology initiatives.
 Prioritize demand and allocate capacity across strategic planning, project assurance, governance, and emerging technology work; establish coverage and knowledge-sharing practices that reduce dependence on individual specialists.
 Manage the function's operating plan, assigned budget, and resources, and build business cases for additional capacity or specialist support.
 3. Architecture Governance and Design Authority 
 Establish security reference architectures, standards, reusable patterns, and guardrails in partnership with global domain architects and enterprise security policy owners.
 Serve as senior security design authority for significant initiatives within the enterprise architecture governance process, with clear decision rights and escalation paths.
 Represent Security Architecture on enterprise technology review boards, resolve cross-domain design issues, and oversee design assurance against approved security requirements.
 Oversee recommendations for architectural exceptions, compensating controls, and remediation plans; escalate material residual risks to accountable business and risk owners through established governance.
 4. Secure Solution Design and Transformation Oversight 
 Provide security architecture oversight for major business and technology initiatives from early planning through implementation, with review effort proportionate to risk and complexity.
 Embed threat modelling, secure design reviews, and reusable security patterns into delivery practices, partnering with application, data, infrastructure, cloud, and engineering teams.
 Lead architectural direction for security transformation programs, including identity modernization, cloud security, network segmentation, application security, data protection, and cyber recovery.
 5. Security Capability Portfolio and Investment Leadership 
 Direct the strategic evolution, integration, consolidation, and retirement of security tools, services, and capabilities to address enterprise needs and reduce fragmentation.
 Shape investment priorities and present business cases that assess risk reduction, control coverage, technical feasibility, interoperability, operational capacity, and total cost of ownership.
 Maintain an enterprise view of capability gaps, overlapping technologies, lifecycle risks, and technical debt; partner with engineering, operations, procurement, and vendor management to turn roadmaps into achievable investment and delivery plans.
 6. Technology Evaluation and AI Security 
 Evaluate emerging security technologies, vendor capabilities, and service models, providing recommendations on suitability, integration, scalability, and long-term viability.
 Sponsor proofs of concept with clear success criteria for security effectiveness, technical compatibility, operational readiness, and business value.
 Define security architecture requirements and patterns for AI platforms, generative AI, and autonomous agents, addressing identity, data access, tool permissions, monitoring, and human oversight.
 Identify opportunities to use automation and AI within security capabilities, working with responsible teams to validate benefits, control effectiveness, and operational accountability.
 7. Architectural Risk and Resilience 
 Identify systemic security architecture weaknesses and drive mitigation roadmaps with accountable engineering, platform, and business technology owners.
 Translate security, privacy, regulatory, and data residency requirements into architecture requirements in partnership with Risk, Compliance, Privacy, and Legal.
 Integrate requirements for resilience, ransomware containment, recovery, logging, and monitoring into security designs, working with operational owners to establish implementation and validation expectations.
 Use findings from incidents, security testing, audits, and control assessments to improve reference architectures, patterns, and capability roadmaps.
 8. Executive Engagement and Enterprise Partnership 
 Act as a trusted advisor to the Global Chief Enterprise Architect, CISO, CTO, CIO, and business technology leaders on security architecture strategy and significant technology decisions.
 Translate complex architecture choices into clear business implications, investment options, delivery dependencies, and risk treatment recommendations for executive forums.
 Build alignment across global business units and technology functions, resolve competing priorities, and report on architecture coverage, adoption, roadmap progress, and outcomes.
 What Do You Need to Succeed? 
 Qualifications Required: 
 University degree or college diploma in cybersecurity, computer science, information technology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
 15+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity architecture, engineering, or related technology leadership roles, including accountability for enterprise security architecture strategy.
 Demonstrated experience leading and developing architecture or security teams, managing priorities and resources, and delivering outcomes in a complex, matrixed organization.
 Experience influencing VP and SVP stakeholders and presenting architecture strategies, investment recommendations, and risk decisions at executive forums.
 Strong knowledge across identity and access management, cloud, infrastructure, network, endpoint, application, API, and data security, including cryptography and secrets management.
 Demonstrated ability to establish enterprise architecture standards, reference patterns, governance processes, and multi-year security capability roadmaps.
 Practical understanding of Zero Trust, defense in depth, threat modelling, secure development, and frameworks such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
 Experience modernizing security platforms and evaluating vendors or third-party services for technical feasibility, integration, control effectiveness, and total cost of ownership.
 Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, with the judgment to balance security, business value, delivery constraints, and operational sustainability.
 Preferred skills: 
 Experience in financial services or another regulated industry with global operations and complex privacy or data residency requirements.
 Experience with hybrid and multi-cloud environments, including AWS, Azure, or Alibaba Cloud.
 Experience defining security architectures for AI, autonomous agents, automation, or other emerging technologies.
 Experience with major security transformations, technology rationalization, or mergers and acquisitions integration.
 Relevant professional certifications, such as CISSP, CISM, SABSA, TOGAF, or cloud security and architecture certifications.
 Key Outcomes and Measures of Success: 
 Enterprise direction: Approved security target states and prioritized roadmaps aligned with business needs and the cybersecurity strategy.
 Architecture coverage: Timely engagement on significant initiatives across business units, with consistent service coverage and review turnaround.
 Secure delivery: Greater use of approved patterns and earlier resolution of design weaknesses, reducing avoidable rework and exceptions.
 Risk treatment: Progress against remediation plans for material architectural weaknesses and timely escalation of unresolved risks.
 Portfolio effectiveness: Reduced capability duplication and technical debt, supported by documented control improvements and lifecycle cost benefits.
 Team capability: Improved skills, succession readiness, knowledge sharing, and capacity to support strategic and delivery priorities.
 Executive confidence: Clear investment recommendations, transparent reporting, and alignment among security, enterprise architecture, and business leaders.

ABOUT GEORGIAN



Georgian is a Toronto-based venture capital firm that partners with high-growth technology companies across cybersecurity, AI software, robotics, defense. We manage about $6B in assets and we have invested in more than 80 companies that we support with capital and technical capability.



Our in-house AI lab works directly with portfolio companies to provide a differentiated experience across the investment lifecycle, and drives the adoption of AI for our internal operations.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE



Are you an aspiring AI Engineer eager to gain real-world impact and learn how to push AI's boundaries? Imagine diving into diverse, cutting-edge AI problems across multiple high-growth companies with the support of a leading VC firm. That's Georgian.



We're not your typical VC. Georgian's unique R&D team partners directly with our portfolio companies, providing the technical horsepower and strategic guidance to help accelerate their AI initiatives. We also play a critical role in our investment process, conducting deep technical diligence to identify promising AI-driven businesses.



Think of it as working in a dynamic startup environment, but without the inherent risks of a single venture. You'll tackle fascinating challenges, meet and potentially work with brilliant founders and CTOs, and try to help unearth the next generation of industry leaders. It's a fun, engaging, and highly impactful way to build your career.




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS



Georgian's mission is to empower the world's leading B2B software companies with an unfair advantage, accelerating their participation in the digital economy. As an AI Engineer Intern on our R&D team, you'll support this mission by contributing to cutting-edge machine learning projects. You'll assist in bringing machine learning expertise directly to our portfolio companies' most pressing challenges, helping them build and scale potentially transformative AI products. You'll also contribute to our investment process technical diligence, helping us identify innovative and technically sound companies.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN & DELIVER



 - Support AI system development. Assist in building LLM agents, Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines and fine‑tuned domain‑specific models under guidance; help implement workflows with frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex/PydanticAI.

 - Contribute to portfolio projects. Support Georgian "strike teams" embedded in portfolio companies; assist with code implementation, testing, and documentation.

 - Technical analysis & documentation. Help convert technical concepts into clear documentation; support preparation of demos and presentations for stakeholders.

 - Hands‑on R&D support. Assist in rapid prototyping, run experiments and ablation studies, contribute to internal tech notes and documentation.

 - Support AI roadmap development. Help gather requirements in discovery workshops, assist in documenting technical specifications and implementation plans.

 - Contribute to safety & governance. Assist in implementing evaluation pipelines and testing frameworks to keep models reliable and compliant.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR




IDEAL ATTRIBUTES

 - Education & Experience: Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master's or PhD degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Statistics, or a related quantitative discipline with a focus on machine learning, optimization theory, or related areas.

 - Hands-On Foundation: Familiarity with deep learning toolkits such as Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch. Understanding of GenAI, LLM tooling and Context Engineering fundamentals.

 - Software Development: Proficiency in Python and foundational software development skills, enabling you to write clean, efficient code.

 - Problem Formulation & Communication: The ability to understand applied research problems, assist in designing experiments, implement solutions, and clearly document findings for diverse audiences with varying technical backgrounds.

 - Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to work on team projects, collaborate effectively with technical groups, and communicate progress to mentors and stakeholders.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience contributing to open-source AI/ML-related projects or research papers.

 - Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) for MLOps and model deployment.

 - Exposure to specific industry verticals relevant to Georgian's portfolio (e.g., vertical SaaS, cybersecurity, healthcare tech, fintech).




CULTURAL ATTRIBUTES WE LOVE



 - High ambition & agency: You're allergic to incrementalism and thrive in low‑structure, high‑ownership settings.

 - Insatiable curiosity: You debug the root cause and ask why until everyone else gets annoyed—in a good way.

 - Team over ego: You amplify colleagues and founders alike, seeing leverage in elevating the collective.

 - Commercial storytelling: You speak with brevity and distill complexity so a time‑starved CEO instantly sees value.




HIRING PROCESS



We don't hire like a MAG7 or scale up — in fact we rarely hire compared to them.



You shouldn't expect a cookie-cutter high-volume hiring process with us — but a more boutique one that allows you to see a lot of the organization before joining us.



We build a thesis in what an individual brings to our very small team, versus simply matching qualifications:

 1. 30‑min intro (values & motivations)

 2. 60‑min technical interview (ML fundamentals & problem‑solving)

 3. Project discussion with team members




POSITION STATUS

 

This posting represents an active, future internship vacancy on our team. We will be interviewing for this role in early 2027.

 


OUR COMMITMENT TO ACCESSIBILITY



Georgian is dedicated to building an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. We provide reasonable accommodations throughout our recruitment process to ensure every candidate has the opportunity to perform at their best. If you require any specific accommodations at any stage, please reach out to us at peopleteam [at]  georgian.io.




USE OF AI



Innovation is at our core and we use artificial intelligence (AI) to support parts of our hiring process, such as screening and evaluating applications. These tools are designed to assist - not replace - human decision making and all final hiring decisions are made by our team.  We regularly review our AI tools to help promote fairness and reduce the risk of unintended bias. If you have any questions about how we use AI in our process or would like more information, please contact us at careers [at] georgian.io.

About Moment Energy 
 Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it. 
 Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone. 
 The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy. 
 Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact. 
 We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale. 
 Now is the moment. Join us. 
 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a detail-oriented and hands-on Mechanical (Thermal/Vibration) Test Engineer to join our dynamic team. This role is crucial for ensuring the safety, reliability, and performance of our innovative battery energy storage systems (BESS). You will spend the majority of your time (80%+) in the R&D and production lab, setting up, running, and analyzing a wide variety of tests that support mechanical and thermal subsystems. You will be expected to own Thermal, Vibration & Shock testing from start to finish including thermal chamber setup, fixture design for component and sub-system level tests that simulate real world temperature and vibration profiles we see in the field. Your work will directly contribute to our product development, certification, and overall success. If you are passionate about clean technology and thrive in a hands-on, fast-paced environment, this is the role for you.
 Responsibilities and Duties 
 Develop, execute, and document comprehensive test plans for various needs, including certification, compliance, R&D, component validation, and lifecycle testing.
 Take primary ownership of hands-on test setup, including setting up fixtures, wiring thermocouples and accelerometers, power supplies, cameras, and cooling bench setups.
 Own vibration and shock testing from start to finish: define the profiles (sine, random, and shock), design fixtures, place accelerometers, collaborate with third party companies to run tests, and investigate failures.
 Perform thermal chamber tests, including setting up controllers, wiring thermocouples, and running cooling plates, chillers, flow and pressure-drop measurements.
 3D CAD design of test fixtures including modal analysis, sized for the shaker table’s capacity and with resonances kept outside the test frequency range.
 Manage 2D manufacturing drawings and fixture fabrication for testing subassemblies and single components, working with both in-house fabrication resources and external vendors. 
 Set up and configure data acquisition systems (DAQ) for data capture of various signals (temperature, humidity, voltage, current, etc.)
 Configure and run scripts for automating test equipment, data gathering, and long-term tests.
 Support the team with abuse testing, including sample preparation and test setup coordination.
 Maintain, troubleshoot, and calibrate lab test equipment to ensure accuracy and reliability.
 Contribute to the creation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for testing and lab activities.

 We’re looking for individuals with the following traits, skills, and experiences: 
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field.
 3+ years of experience in a hands-on testing, validation, or verification role.
 Hands-on experience running vibration and shock tests (shaker tables, vibration controllers, accelerometers). 
 Proficiency in 3D CAD (Fusion, SolidWorks, Onshape, or similar), with a track record of designing fixtures or hardware that was built and used. 
 Proven ability to create test plans, design experiments, and document results.
 Hands-on proficiency in common machine shop tools such as mill, drill press, tap and die, plasma cutter, and mechanical assembly of fixtures.
 Nice-to-Have Experience: 
 Experience with data capture/data acquisition systems, test automation, or data visualization and analysis using scripting languages like Python or command interfaces like SCPI.
 Experience with lithium-ion battery systems, battery cyclers, and battery management systems (BMS).
 Knowledge of safety and compliance standards for batteries and energy storage, such as UL1973 or UL9540.
 Familiarity with liquid cooling or other thermal management systems. 
 Why join us? 
 Today, we’re delivering 5x the energy density and have all the certifications needed to ship energy independence to the world. 
 Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world. 
 Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence. 
 Contribute to building and scaling a company from the ground up, where your work will have a direct and meaningful impact. 
 Thrive in a workplace that values collaboration, wellness, and celebrating successes, with regular company socials, fitness sessions, and more. 
 We're a fast-paced and dynamic team. 
 Every day you'll be taking on a new challenge and learning something new. You'll take on a wide breadth of tasks and contribute to disrupting the battery industry. You'll be part of a tight-knit team that is working together to save the planet! Fun, health, and wellness are incorporated into our daily schedule and we encourage all our team members to bring innovative ideas to the table to create an interactive workplace.

 Financial Growth: Employee equity and a robust RRSP matching program.

 Own and evolve our software engineering practice , establishing clear standards, processes and expectations that improve consistency, quality and accountability.

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation.  An overview of this role 
 As a Senior Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Security team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write and in the open source components they depend on.
 Your work spans complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the dependency analysis side, you teach the analysis engine what a project depends on. You parse dependency manifests, lockfiles, and SBOMs so the engine knows which libraries and frameworks are in play and how the code uses them. You also extend the service that turns security advisories into automated merge requests that update vulnerable dependencies. On the vulnerability detection side, you grow GitLab's security analysis engine with hybrid analyzers that blend rule-based detection and AI reasoning. You build and apply the tooling that develops, evaluates, and ships those analyzers, and you measure how well they find real problems. That work also expands coverage of the libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling that real-world applications are built on.
 These threads reinforce each other. What a project depends on, and how its code uses those dependencies, are parts of one picture, and this team works across all of it. We make thoughtful use of AI-assisted development tools in our daily work. We expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.
 What you do 
 Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for team initiatives from design through delivery, shipping with minimal guidance in partnership with the technical lead
 Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review
 Design and ship analyzers that pair deterministic analysis capabilities with AI-driven analysis, and build the evaluation harnesses that measure their false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes detection rules mapped to CWE and the test fixtures that prove they work.
 Package those analyzers for every place GitLab runs them, including CI jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, with findings reported in GitLab's standard security report formats
 Design and ship the manifest, lockfile, and SBOM parsing that tells the static analysis engine what a project depends on, and extend it to new ecosystems and formats
 Ship features across the automated remediation service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, from sandboxed updates to merge request creation
 Solve technical problems of high scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, Engineering stakeholders such as Frontend and UX, and partner teams such as Code Scanning and Composition Analysis
 Mentor Intermediate engineers through code review and pairing, and maintain our internal standards for style, maintainability, and best practices through review
 Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues
 Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it
 What you bring 
 Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't
 Substantial professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Go and/or Rust, with depth in at least one. We use both, plus Ruby on the remediation side and Python for some analyzers, and value willingness to work across them.
 Familiarity with package managers and dependency management in one or more language ecosystems, such as npm, Maven, pip, Bundler, or Cargo. Experience building tooling around them is better still.
 Demonstrated application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE) and the software supply chain

 Helpful experience

 Experience with performance optimization at scale

We help developers find and fix security issues in both the code they write and the open source components they depend on, as early as possible.

L'entrée en poste du Leader en formation se fera en débutant avec notre programme de développement. Cet apprentissage vise à former les futurs gestionnaires de première ligne qui joueront un rôle essentiel dans la direction de nos équipes et dans la recherche et l'atteinte de l'excellence opérationnelle. Ce programme offre une occasion unique de renforcer vos compétences en gestion, d'acquérir des connaissances approfondies du monde des affaires et de faire progresser votre carrière au sein de notre organisation. Le leader en formation aura l'occasion de travailler dans diverses succursales situées dans les provinces du Québec (par exemple, sur la Rive-Sud, à Drummondville et à Sherbrooke)
 Le programme de formation sera proposé pour une durée maximale de 6 mois. Les participants effectueront une rotation dans tous les principaux services et sites, afin d'acquérir des compétences et des connaissances sur ces différentes sphères telles que : 
 Centre d’appels – Acquérir une compréhension approfondie du processus d’achat d’une voiture. 
 Répartition – Acquérir une compréhension approfondie du processus de récupération des voitures sur les sites. 
 Achat et vente de véhicules – Comprendre le processus d’achat de véhicules en succursale. 
 Marketing – Acquérir une compréhension de la manière dont nous effectuons la promotion de nos produits. 
 Service client – Élaborer des stratégies visant à améliorer la satisfaction de la clientèle, à résoudre efficacement les problèmes de service et à renforcer les relations clients. 
 Opérations – Acquérir une compréhension approfondie de nos processus opérationnels et de vente au détail (y compris les opérations dans la cour et le processus de dépollution). 
 Systèmes et outils – Démonstration des systèmes et des programmes, et vérification que les droits d’accès sont bien accordés. 
 Enquêtes sur les accidents et les blessures – Soutenir la direction dans les enquêtes sur les incidents survenus sur le lieu de travail, consigner les conclusions et contribuer à l’élaboration de plans d’actions correctives visant à renforcer les protocoles de sécurité. 
 Formation – Suivre la formation obligatoire sur AIM Campus. 
 Santé et sécurité – Acquérir une compréhension approfondie de la conformité réglementaire, de la gestion des risques et des pratiques de sécurité proactives. 
 Il s’agit d’un programme pratique, sur le terrain, où la majeure partie de la journée est consacrée à travailler directement avec les employés de première ligne. Le leader en formation acquerra une expérience pratique en matière d’accompagnement, de mentorat et d’encadrement d’équipes diversifiées, tout en renforçant les normes les plus strictes en matière de sécurité et de conformité. 
 À l'issue de la formation, les participants seront capables de : 
 Diriger les opérations d'une succursale, notamment la gestion de la cour et la dépollution. 
 Diriger les activités de vente au détail d’une succursale, notamment en accompagnant les clients tout au long de leur achat — de la localisation des produits sur le site à la recommandation d’options de garantie adaptées. 
 Accompagner les transactions d’achat et de vente de véhicules en veillant au respect de toutes les procédures et à la bonne constitution des dossiers requis. 
 Identifier et consulter efficacement les informations pertinentes tout en s’assurant que tous les dossiers et procédures requis sont bien constitués. 
 Encadrer et soutenir les collaborateurs dans leurs activités quotidiennes afin de garantir l’efficacité opérationnelle et l’excellence du service.

 Vous êtes diplômé d’un établissement d’enseignement supérieur, d’une université ou d’un centre de formation professionnelle.

We always place every client at the centre of our approach to care, based on their needs. We address these needs through integrated clinical and wellness care and health education.
 It's an exciting time to be joining this organization.  Durham Community Health Centre has been selected as the lead agency for the new Homeless Addiction Recovery Treatment (HART) Hub in the Durham region.  This innovative hub will provide life-changing services for individuals struggling with addiction and mental health challenges, helping them regain stability and rebuild their futures. Cohere's North team is seeking a Software Engineer with a focus on security to join our mission and make a significant impact.  - Have worked across GCP, AWS, Azure, or hybrid/multi-cloud deployments

 - Are comfortable working across the stack

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!



Role Overview:

Contribute in and provide strong support for model training pipelines, ship state of the art models to production, and bridge the gap between research and production. We have one of the highest ratio of compute to engineers in the world. We do not delineate strongly between engineering and research. Everyone will contribute to writing production code and supporting our research effort depending on individual interest and organizational needs. We have all the compute, data, and talent available for you to do your best work.

Please Note: We have offices in London, Paris, Toronto, San Francisco and New York but also embrace being remote-friendly! There are no restrictions on where you can be located for this role.



Key Responsibilities:

 - Design and write high-performant and scalable software for training. 

 - Improve our training setup from an infrastructure and codebase performance standpoint.

 - Craft and implement tools to speed up our training cycles and improve the overall efficacy of our training infrastructure

 - Research, implement, and experiment with ideas on our supercompute and data infrastructure.

 - Learn from and work with the best researchers in the field.



Qualifications:

 - Extremely strong software engineering skills.

 - Proficiency in Python and related ML frameworks such as JAX, Pytorch and XLA/MLIR.

 - Experience with distributed training infrastructures (Kubernetes, Slurm) and associated frameworks (Ray)

 - Experience using large-scale distributed training strategies.

 - Hands on experience on training large model at scale and having contributed to the tooling and/or setup of the training infrastructure

 - Bonus: paper at top-tier venues (such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AIStats, MLSys, JMLR, AAAI, Nature, COLING, ACL, EMNLP).



Working Location:
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.
